title: 2023年全国甲卷英语（笔试部分）
answerSource: 2023年全国甲卷英语解析版（含逐题详解）
note: 本卷仅收录笔试部分（阅读、语言知识运用、写作），共52题120分，题号按解析版编号（阅读从1开始）。原因：解析版虽重排了20道听力题的题干与选项，但答案块从阅读第1题起，通篇无听力答案，也无听力原文与音频，详见《题库待补清单.md》。源文档存在若干 OCR 错字（如 Issays Stamese Club / Loodon-based / word's 50 best / sence / lates / undestanding 等），录入时已按原卷正确拼写修正。

sections.partTitle: 第二部分 阅读理解（共两节，满分40分）
sections.secTitle: 第一节（共15小题；每小题2分，满分30分）阅读下列短文，从每题所给的A、B、C和D四个选项中，选出最佳选项。

passages.label: A
passages.text:
Where to Eat in Bangkok

Bangkok is a highly desirable destination for food lovers. It has a seemingly bottomless well of dining options. Here are some suggestions on where to start your Bangkok eating adventure.

Nahm
Offering Thai fine dining, Nahm provides the best of Bangkok culinary (烹饪的) experiences. It's the only Thai restaurant that ranks among the top 10 of the world's 50 best restaurants list. Head Chef David Thompson, who received a Michelin star for his London-based Thai restaurant of the same name, opened this branch in the Metropolitan Hotel in 2010.

Issaya Siamese Club
Issaya Siamese Club is internationally known Thai chef Ian Kittichai's first flagship Bangkok restaurant. The menu in this beautiful colonial house includes traditional Thai cuisine combined with modern cooking methods.

Bo.lan
Bo.lan has been making waves in Bangkok's culinary scene since it opened in 2009. Serving hard-to-find Thai dishes in an elegant atmosphere, the restaurant is true to Thai cuisine's roots, yet still manages to add a special twist. This place is good for a candlelit dinner or a work meeting with colleagues who appreciate fine food. For those extremely hungry there's a large set menu.

Gaggan
Earning first place on the latest "Asia's 50 best restaurants" list, progressive Indian restaurant Gaggan is one of the most exciting venues (场所) to arrive in Bangkok in recent years. The best table in this two-story colonial Thai home offers a window right into the kitchen, where you can see chef Gaggan and his staff in action. Culinary theater at its best.

passages.label: B
passages.text:
Terri Bolton is a dab hand when it comes to DIY (do-it-yourself). Skilled at putting up shelves and piecing together furniture, she never pays someone else to do a job she can do herself.

She credits these skills to her late grandfather and builder Derek Lloyd. From the age of six, Terri, now 26, accompanied Derek to work during her school holidays. A day's work was rewarded with £5 in pocket money. She says: "I'm sure I wasn't much of a help to start with, painting the rooms and putting down the flooring throughout the house. It took weeks and it was backbreaking work, but I know he was proud of my skills."

Terri, who now rents a house with friends in Wandsworth, South West London, says DIY also saves her from losing any deposit when a tenancy (租期) comes to an end. She adds: "I've moved house many times and I always like to personalise my room and put up pictures. So, it's been useful to know how to cover up holes and repaint a room to avoid any charges when I've moved out."

With millions of people likely to take on DIY projects over the coming weeks, new research shows that more than half of people are planning to make the most of the long, warm summer days to get jobs done. The average spend per project will be around £823. Two thirds of people aim to improve their comfort while at home. Two fifths wish to increase the value of their house. Though DIY has traditionally been seen as a male hobby, the research shows it is women now leading the charge.

passages.label: C
passages.text:
I was about 13 when an uncle gave me a copy of Jostein Gaarder's Sophie's World. It was full of ideas that were new to me, so I spent the summer with my head in and out of that book. It spoke to me and brought me into a world of philosophy (哲学).

That love for philosophy lasted until I got to college. Nothing kills the love for philosophy faster than people who think they understand Foucault, Baudrillard, or Confucius better than you — and then try to explain them.

Eric Weiner's The Socrates Express: In Search of Life Lessons from Dead Philosophers reawakened my love for philosophy. It is not an explanation, but an invitation to think and experience philosophy.

Weiner starts each chapter with a scene on a train ride between cities and then frames each philosopher's work in the context (背景) of one thing they can help us do better. The end result is a read in which we learn to wonder like Socrates, see like Thoreau, listen like Schopenhauer, and have no regrets like Nietzsche. This, more than a book about understanding philosophy, is a book about learning to use philosophy to improve a life.

He makes philosophical thought an appealing exercise that improves the quality of our experiences, and he does so with plenty of humor. Weiner enters into conversation with some of the most important philosophers in history, and he becomes part of that crowd in the process by decoding (解读) their messages and adding his own interpretation.

The Socrates Express is a fun, sharp book that draws readers in with its apparent simplicity and gradually pulls them in deeper thoughts on desire, loneliness, and aging. The invitation is clear: Weiner wants you to pick up a coffee or tea and sit down with this book. I encourage you to take his offer. It's worth your time, even if time is something we don't have a lot of.

passages.label: D
passages.text:
Grizzly bears, which may grow to about 2.5 m long and weigh over 400 kg, occupy a conflicted corner of the American psyche — we revere (敬畏) them even as they give us frightening dreams. Ask the tourists from around the world that flood into Yellowstone National Park what they most hope to see, and their answer is often the same: a grizzly bear.

"Grizzly bears are re-occupying large areas of their former range," says bear biologist Chris Servheen. As grizzly bears expand their range into places where they haven't been seen in a century or more, they're increasingly being sighted by humans.

The western half of the U.S. was full of grizzlies when Europeans came, with a rough number of 50,000 or more living alongside Native Americans. By the early 1970s, after centuries of cruel and continuous hunting by settlers, 600 to 800 grizzlies remained on a mere 2 percent of their former range in the Northern Rockies. In 1975, grizzlies were listed under the Endangered Species Act.

Today, there are about 2,000 or more grizzly bears in the U.S. Their recovery has been so successful that the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service has twice attempted to delist grizzlies, which would loosen legal protections and allow them to be hunted. Both efforts were overturned due to lawsuits from conservation groups. For now, grizzlies remain listed.

Obviously, if precautions (预防) aren't taken, grizzlies can become troublesome, sometimes killing farm animals or walking through yards in search of food. If people remove food and attractants from their yards and campsites, grizzlies will typically pass by without trouble. Putting electric fencing around chicken houses and other farm animal quarters is also highly effective at getting grizzlies away. "Our hope is to have a clean, attractant-free place where bears can pass through without learning bad habits," says James Jonkel, longtime biologist who manages bears in and around Missoula.

questions.stem: What do Nahm and Issaya Siamese Club have in common?

explanation.summary: 细节理解题｜本文是应用文，介绍在曼谷从哪几家餐厅开始美食之旅。
explanation.question: 问 Nahm 和 Issaya Siamese Club 的共同之处。
explanation.evidence: Head Chef David Thompson, who received a Michelin star for his London-based Thai restaurant of the same name…／Issaya Siamese Club is internationally known Thai chef Ian Kittichai's first flagship Bangkok restaurant.
explanation.answer: C。前者的主厨拿过米其林一星，后者出自国际知名泰国厨师之手，共同点是都有一流厨师。伦敦那家是同名餐厅而非分店（B），只有 Nahm 开在酒店里（D）。

questions.stem: Which restaurant offers a large set menu?

explanation.summary: 细节理解题｜定位小标题 Bo.lan。
explanation.question: 问哪家餐厅提供大份套餐。
explanation.evidence: For those extremely hungry there's a large set menu.
explanation.answer: B。该句出现在 Bo.lan 一段，故答案为 Bo.lan。

questions.stem: What is special about Gaggan?

options.text: It puts on a play every day.
It shows the cooking process to guests.

explanation.summary: 细节理解题｜定位小标题 Gaggan。
explanation.question: 问 Gaggan 的特别之处。
explanation.evidence: The best table in this two-story colonial Thai home offers a window right into the kitchen, where you can see chef Gaggan and his staff in action.
explanation.answer: D。最好的座位有一扇直通厨房的窗，客人能看到烹饪全过程。末句 Culinary theater 是比喻说法，并非真的每天演戏（B）；提供难寻本地菜的是 Bo.lan（C）。

questions.stem: Which is closest in meaning to "a dab hand" in paragraph 1?

explanation.summary: 词句猜测题｜本文是记叙文，讲 DIY 高手 Terri Bolton，并指出 DIY 正在女性中流行。
explanation.question: 问第一段 a dab hand 的意思最接近哪一项。
explanation.evidence: Skilled at putting up shelves and piecing together furniture, she never pays someone else to do a job she can do herself.
explanation.answer: C。下文说她擅长装架子、拼家具，从不花钱请人做自己能做的活，可见 a dab hand 意为「行家、高手」，与 A specialist 最接近。

questions.stem: Why did Terri's grandfather give her £5 a day?

options.text: As a treat for her work.
To encourage her to take up a hobby.

explanation.question: 问她祖父为什么每天给她 5 英镑。
explanation.evidence: A day's work was rewarded with £5 in pocket money…It took weeks and it was backbreaking work, but I know he was proud of my skills.
explanation.answer: B。一天的活儿换来 5 英镑零花钱，是对她劳动的奖励（a treat for her work）。

questions.stem: How did Terri avoid losing the deposit on the house she rented?

options.text: By making it look like before.
By splitting the rent with a roommate.

explanation.question: 问她如何避免押金被扣。
explanation.evidence: it's been useful to know how to cover up holes and repaint a room to avoid any charges when I've moved out
explanation.answer: A。她会补好钉孔、重新刷墙，把房间恢复原样，从而避免被扣费。

questions.stem: What trend in DIY does the research show?

options.text: It is turning into a seasonal industry.
It is gaining popularity among females.

explanation.question: 问研究显示 DIY 的什么趋势。
explanation.evidence: Though DIY has traditionally been seen as a male hobby, the research shows it is women now leading the charge.
explanation.answer: D。DIY 素来被视为男性爱好，但研究显示如今是女性在引领潮流，即在女性中日益流行。

questions.stem: Who opened the door to philosophy for the author?

explanation.summary: 细节理解题｜本文是书评，作者由《苏菲的世界》爱上哲学，又被 Weiner 的书重新点燃热情。
explanation.question: 问是谁为作者打开了哲学之门。
explanation.evidence: an uncle gave me a copy of Jostein Gaarder's Sophie's World…It spoke to me and brought me into a world of philosophy
explanation.answer: C。是 Jostein Gaarder 的《苏菲的世界》把作者带进哲学世界；Eric Weiner（B）是后来「重新唤起」他热情的人，并非最初的引路人。

questions.stem: Why does the author list great philosophers in paragraph 4?

options.text: To give examples of great works.
To help readers understand Weiner's book.

explanation.summary: 推理判断题｜第四段的写作意图。
explanation.question: 问作者在第四段列举众多哲学家的目的。
explanation.evidence: The end result is a read in which we learn to wonder like Socrates, see like Thoreau, listen like Schopenhauer, and have no regrets like Nietzsche.
explanation.answer: D。作者先介绍该书结构，再用「像苏格拉底一样思考、像梭罗一样观察」等具体说明读者能学到什么，目的是帮助读者理解 Weiner 这本书。

questions.stem: What does the author like about The Socrates Express?

options.text: Its views on history are well-presented.
Its ideas can be applied to daily life.

explanation.summary: 细节理解题｜第四段末句。
explanation.question: 问作者喜欢这本书的哪一点。
explanation.evidence: This, more than a book about understanding philosophy, is a book about learning to use philosophy to improve a life.
explanation.answer: B。它不只是讲「理解哲学」，更是教人「用哲学改善生活」，即书中观点可用于日常生活。

questions.stem: What does the author think of Weiner's book?

explanation.summary: 推理判断题｜倒数两段的评价。
explanation.question: 问作者如何评价 Weiner 的书。
explanation.evidence: he does so with plenty of humor／a fun, sharp book that draws readers in with its apparent simplicity
explanation.answer: D。既「充满幽默」，又「以表面的简单吸引读者」，故是幽默而直白易读；C 与 hard to follow 相悖。

questions.stem: How do Americans look at grizzlies?

options.text: They cause mixed feelings in people.
They should be kept in national parks.
They are of high scientific value.
They are a symbol of American culture.

explanation.summary: 细节理解题｜本文是说明文，讲美国灰熊从濒危到恢复及随之而来的人熊共处问题。
explanation.question: 问美国人如何看待灰熊。
explanation.evidence: occupy a conflicted corner of the American psyche — we revere them even as they give us frightening dreams
explanation.answer: A。灰熊在美国人心中占据一个「矛盾的角落」——既敬畏又害怕，故是引发复杂情感。

questions.stem: What has helped the increase of the grizzly population?

explanation.summary: 推理判断题｜第三、四段的因果关系。
explanation.question: 问什么促成了灰熊数量的增长。
explanation.evidence: In 1975, grizzlies were listed under the Endangered Species Act.／Today, there are about 2,000 or more grizzly bears in the U.S.
explanation.answer: C。1975 年被列入《濒危物种法》受法律保护后，数量由 600—800 头回升到 2000 多头。栖息地扩张（B）是数量恢复的结果而非原因。

questions.stem: What has stopped the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service from delisting grizzlies?

explanation.question: 问什么阻止了鱼类和野生动物管理局把灰熊除名。
explanation.evidence: Both efforts were overturned due to lawsuits from conservation groups. For now, grizzlies remain listed.
explanation.answer: A。两次除名尝试都因环保组织提起诉讼而被推翻，即环保团体的反对。

questions.stem: What can be inferred from the last paragraph?

options.text: Food should be provided for grizzlies.
People can live in harmony with grizzlies.
A special path should be built for grizzlies.
Technology can be introduced to protect grizzlies.

explanation.question: 问从最后一段可以推断出什么。
explanation.evidence: If people remove food and attractants from their yards and campsites, grizzlies will typically pass by without trouble.／"Our hope is to have a clean, attractant-free place where bears can pass through without learning bad habits"
explanation.answer: B。只要采取移走食物、加装电围栏等预防措施，灰熊通常会安然经过，可推知人与灰熊能够和谐共处。A 与「移走食物」正相反。

sections.partTitle: 第二部分 阅读理解（共两节，满分40分）
sections.secTitle: 第二节（共5小题；每小题2分，满分10分）根据短文内容，从短文后的选项中选出能填入空白处的最佳选项。选项中有两项为多余选项。

pool.text: All this adds up to a state of hurry
It can also help us practice more patience
This is merely uncomfortable, not intolerable
They're all situations where we could use a little extra patience

passages.label: 七选五
passages.text:
Tricks To Becoming A Patient Person

Here's a riddle: What do traffic jams, long lines and waiting for a vacation to start all have in common? There's one answer. ___16___.

In the Digital Age, we're used to having what we need immediately and right at our fingertips. However, research suggests that if we practiced patience, we'd be a whole lot better off. Here are several tricks.

● Practice gratitude (感激)
Thankfulness has a lot of benefits: Research shows it makes us happier, less stressed and even more optimistic. ___17___. "Showing thankfulness can foster self-control," said Ye Li, researcher at the University of California.

● Make yourself wait
Instant gratification (满足) may seem like the most "feel good" option at the time, but psychology research suggests waiting for things actually makes us happier in the long run. And the only way for us to get into the habit of waiting is to practice. ___18___. Put off watching your favorite show until the weekend or wait 10 extra minutes before going for that cake. You'll soon find that the more patience you practice, the more you start to apply it to other, more annoying situations.

● ___19___.
So many of us have the belief that being comfortable is the only state we will tolerate, and when we experience something outside of our comfort zone, we get impatient about the circumstances. You should learn to say to yourself, "___20___." You'll then gradually become more patient.

explanation.summary: 本文是说明文，介绍成为一个耐心的人的几个技巧。
explanation.question: 空格承接上文的「谜语」，需给出答案。
explanation.evidence: Here's a riddle: What do traffic jams, long lines and waiting for a vacation to start all have in common? There's one answer.
explanation.answer: G。交通堵塞、排长队、等假期开始的共同点，正是「都是需要多一点耐心的情形」。

options.text: All this adds up to a state of hurry
It can also help us practice more patience
This is merely uncomfortable, not intolerable
They're all situations where we could use a little extra patience

explanation.summary: 承接「感恩的好处」这一话题。
explanation.question: 空格在列举感恩好处之后、引用研究者的话之前。
explanation.evidence: Thankfulness has a lot of benefits…／"Showing thankfulness can foster self-control," said Ye Li
explanation.answer: E。E 项的 It 指代上文的 Thankfulness，补充「它还能帮我们练习耐心」，与下文「培养自控力」呼应。

options.text: All this adds up to a state of hurry
It can also help us practice more patience
This is merely uncomfortable, not intolerable
They're all situations where we could use a little extra patience

explanation.summary: 承接「养成等待习惯的唯一方法是练习」。
explanation.question: 空格后列举的都是推迟追剧、多等 10 分钟再吃蛋糕这类小事。
explanation.evidence: the only way for us to get into the habit of waiting is to practice.／Put off watching your favorite show until the weekend…
explanation.answer: B。下文都是日常小事，故此处提出「从小任务开始」。

options.text: All this adds up to a state of hurry
It can also help us practice more patience
This is merely uncomfortable, not intolerable
They're all situations where we could use a little extra patience

explanation.question: 根据本段主旨确定小标题，注意前两个小标题均为祈使句。
explanation.evidence: So many of us have the belief that being comfortable is the only state we will tolerate…we get impatient about the circumstances.
explanation.answer: C。本段讲人们只肯忍受舒适、一出舒适区就失去耐心，故小标题为「接受不舒适」，C 项 uncomfortable 与段中 comfortable 对应。

options.text: All this adds up to a state of hurry
It can also help us practice more patience
This is merely uncomfortable, not intolerable
They're all situations where we could use a little extra patience

explanation.summary: 空格是引号内「对自己说的话」。
explanation.question: 需填入一句能帮助自己接受不适的自我对话。
explanation.evidence: You should learn to say to yourself, "___20___." You'll then gradually become more patient.
explanation.answer: F。「这只是不舒服，并非无法忍受」正是接受不适的自我劝导，与本段主题一致。

sections.partTitle: 第三部分 语言知识运用（共两节，满分45分）
sections.secTitle: 第一节（共20小题；每小题1.5分，满分30分）阅读下面短文，从短文后各题所给的A、B、C和D四个选项中，选出可以填入空白处的最佳选项。

passages.label: 完形填空
passages.text:
Many years ago, I bought a house in the Garfagnana, where we still go every summer. The first time we ___21___ there, we heard the chug-chug-chug of a motorbike ___22___ its way down the hill toward us. It was ___23___ called Mario, coming to ___24___ us a box containing some tomatoes and a bottle of wine. It was a very nice ___25___ for him to make. But when we looked at the tomatoes, we were ___26___ because they were so misshapen: not at all like the nice, round, ___27___ things you get in a supermarket. And the wine was cloudy, in a funny old bottle with no label (标签) on it. These can't be any ___28___, we thought. But we were ___29___ his kindness, so we ___30___ them.

What we discovered is that it's ___31___ to judge what you eat only by its ___32___. Those tomatoes had ___33___ that reminded me of the ones my uncle used to grow when I was a child. Nowadays supermarket tomatoes ___34___ perfect but taste of water. Nobody's going to have a ___35___ memory of those. It's a surprise they haven't managed to grow square ones so that they can ___36___ them easily. Mario's wine may have been cloudy and come out of an old bottle, but it was ___37___.

It's good to eat things at the correct time, when they're ___38___, and as close as possible to where they were ___39___. What Mario had ___40___ us was the taste of the Garfagnana.

explanation.summary: 考查动词词义辨析｜本文是记叙文，讲邻居马里奥送来自种西红柿和自酿酒，作者由「以貌取食」到明白外表不等于品质。
explanation.question: 句意：我们第一次住在那里的时候，听到一辆摩托车从山上朝我们开来的嘎吱声。
explanation.evidence: Many years ago, I bought a house in the Garfagnana, where we still go every summer.
explanation.answer: D。既然买了房子，指的就是第一次「住」在那里。wait 等待／meet 遇见／camp 露营均不合。

explanation.summary: 考查动词词义辨析（固定搭配）。
explanation.question: 句意：一辆摩托车从山上朝我们「开」过来。
explanation.evidence: a motorbike ___22___ its way down the hill toward us
explanation.answer: A。make one's way「前往、行进」为固定搭配。

explanation.question: 句意：来人是一位名叫马里奥的「邻居」。
explanation.evidence: we heard the chug-chug-chug of a motorbike…down the hill toward us／What Mario had…us was the taste of the Garfagnana
explanation.answer: B。他从山上下来给作者一家送当地食物，可推知是邻居。

explanation.question: 句意：他来给我们「带」一盒西红柿和一瓶酒。
explanation.evidence: coming to ___24___ us a box containing some tomatoes and a bottle of wine
explanation.answer: C。人亲自骑车前来，用 bring（带来）；send 是「寄送」，不合语境。

explanation.question: 句意：他这么做真是一个很好的「举动」。
explanation.evidence: It was a very nice ___25___ for him to make.
explanation.answer: D。make a nice gesture「表示善意的举动」，指送东西这一友好行为。

explanation.question: 句意：但看到那些西红柿时我们有点「担心」，因为它们奇形怪状。
explanation.evidence: because they were so misshapen: not at all like the nice, round…things you get in a supermarket
explanation.answer: A。西红柿畸形，作者担心能不能吃。

explanation.question: 句意：完全不像超市里那种漂亮、圆润、「油亮」的样子。
explanation.evidence: not at all like the nice, round, ___27___ things you get in a supermarket
explanation.answer: C。与 nice、round 并列描述超市西红柿的外观，shiny（有光泽的）最合。

explanation.question: 句意：我们想，这些肯定「不怎么好」。
explanation.evidence: the tomatoes…were so misshapen／the wine was cloudy, in a funny old bottle with no label on it
explanation.answer: B。西红柿畸形、酒又浑浊无标签，故推测「不可能好」。

explanation.question: 句意：但我们「感谢」他的好意，所以还是尝了尝。
explanation.evidence: But we were ___29___ his kindness, so we ___30___ them.
explanation.answer: B。be thankful for「对……表示感谢」，与 his kindness 搭配。

explanation.question: 句意：所以我们「尝」了尝。
explanation.evidence: Those tomatoes had ___33___ that reminded me of the ones my uncle used to grow
explanation.answer: A。下文写出了尝过后的感受，故此处是 tried（尝试）。

explanation.summary: 考查形容词词义辨析（主旨句）。
explanation.question: 句意：我们发现，仅凭外表判断食物是「不明智的」。
explanation.evidence: it's ___31___ to judge what you eat only by its ___32___
explanation.answer: C。全文正是要说明以貌取食并不明智。

explanation.question: 句意：仅凭「外观」来判断食物。
explanation.evidence: we were…because they were so misshapen
explanation.answer: A。前文因外形畸形而生疑，故此处是 appearance。

explanation.question: 句意：那些西红柿的「味道」让我想起小时候叔叔种的。
explanation.evidence: Nowadays supermarket tomatoes ___34___ perfect but taste of water.
explanation.answer: D。下文用超市西红柿「好看却像水」作对比，故此处强调味道。

explanation.question: 句意：如今超市的西红柿「看起来」完美，却味同白水。
explanation.evidence: not at all like the nice, round…things you get in a supermarket
explanation.answer: B。与后半句 taste of water 构成「外观 vs 味道」的对照，用 look。

explanation.question: 句意：没人会对那种西红柿留下「愉快的」记忆。
explanation.evidence: Nowadays supermarket tomatoes ___34___ perfect but taste of water.
explanation.answer: A。味道如水，自然留不下美好回忆；与上文作者对叔叔西红柿的怀念形成对比。

explanation.question: 句意：奇怪他们还没培育出方形西红柿，好方便「包装」。
explanation.evidence: It's a surprise they haven't managed to grow square ones so that they can ___36___ them easily.
explanation.answer: D。方形便于装箱码放，故用 pack。

explanation.question: 句意：马里奥的酒或许浑浊、装在旧瓶里，但它「好极了」。
explanation.evidence: Mario's wine may have been cloudy and come out of an old bottle, but it was ___37___.
explanation.answer: A。but 表转折，与前面的「浑浊、旧瓶」相对，用 perfect。

explanation.question: 句意：在正确的时间、食物「当季」时吃最好。
explanation.evidence: It's good to eat things at the correct time, when they're ___38___
explanation.answer: C。in season「当令的、应季的」，与 at the correct time 呼应。

explanation.question: 句意：并且尽可能靠近它们「生长」的地方吃。
explanation.evidence: as close as possible to where they were ___39___
explanation.answer: D。where 引导地点，指作物的产地，用 grown。

explanation.summary: 考查动词词义辨析（主旨升华句）。
explanation.question: 句意：马里奥「送给」我们的，是加尔法尼亚纳的味道。
explanation.evidence: It was ___23___ called Mario, coming to ___24___ us a box containing some tomatoes and a bottle of wine.
explanation.answer: B。全文讲他把自家的西红柿和酒送给作者，故用 given。

sections.partTitle: 第三部分 语言知识运用（共两节，满分45分）
sections.secTitle: 第二节（共10小题；每小题1.5分，满分15分）阅读下面短文，在空白处填入1个适当的单词或括号内单词的正确形式。

passages.label: G
passages.text:
For thousands of years people have told fables (寓言) ____41____ (teach) a lesson or to pass on wisdom. Fables were part of the oral tradition of many early cultures, and the well-known Aesop's fables date to the ____42____ (six) century, B.C. Yet, the form of the fable still has values today, ____43____ Rachel Carson says in "A Fable for Tomorrow".

Carson uses a simple, direct style common to fables. In fact, her style and tone (口吻) are seemingly directed at children. "There was once a town in the heart of America, ____44____ all life seemed to enjoy peaceful existence with its surroundings," her fable begins, ____45____ (borrow) some familiar words from many age-old fables. Behind the simple style, however, is a serious message ____46____ (intend) for everyone.

____47____ (difference) from traditional fables, Carson's story ends with an accusation instead of a moral. She warns of the environmental dangers facing society, and she teaches that people must take responsibility ____48____ saving their environment.

The themes of traditional fables often deal with simple truths about everyday life. However, Carson's theme is a more weighty ____49____ (warn) about environmental destruction. Carson proves that a simple lyric form that has been passed down through the ages can still ____50____ (employ) today to draw attention to important truths.

questions.stem: 第41空（teach）

explanation.summary: 考查非谓语动词｜本文是说明文，说明寓言这一文体在今天依然有价值。
explanation.question: 句意：几千年来人们讲寓言以传授道理或传递智慧。
explanation.evidence: people have told fables ____41____ (teach) a lesson or to pass on wisdom
explanation.answer: to teach。与后面的 or to pass on 并列，用动词不定式作目的状语。

questions.stem: 第42空（six）

explanation.question: 句意：著名的伊索寓言可追溯到公元前 6 世纪。
explanation.evidence: date to the ____42____ (six) century, B.C.
explanation.answer: sixth。century 前表示第几世纪须用序数词。

questions.stem: 第43空

explanation.question: 句意：正如 Rachel Carson 在《明日寓言》中所说，寓言的形式今天仍有价值。
explanation.evidence: the form of the fable still has values today, ____43____ Rachel Carson says in "A Fable for Tomorrow"
explanation.answer: as。表示「正如」，引导非限制性定语从句。

questions.stem: 第44空

explanation.question: 句意：从前美国腹地有一个小镇，那里万物似乎都与周围环境和谐共处。
explanation.evidence: There was once a town in the heart of America, ____44____ all life seemed to enjoy peaceful existence with its surroundings
explanation.answer: where。先行词 town 是地点，从句中缺地点状语，用关系副词 where。

questions.stem: 第45空（borrow）

explanation.question: 句意：她的寓言这样开头，借用了许多古老寓言中熟悉的措辞。
explanation.evidence: her fable begins, ____45____ (borrow) some familiar words
explanation.answer: borrowing。句中已有谓语 begins，逻辑主语 her fable 与 borrow 是主动关系，用现在分词作状语。

questions.stem: 第46空（intend）

explanation.question: 句意：在朴素文风背后，是一则面向所有人的严肃讯息。
explanation.evidence: is a serious message ____46____ (intend) for everyone
explanation.answer: intended。be intended for「专为……而准备」，此处用过去分词短语作后置定语。

questions.stem: 第47空（difference）

explanation.question: 句意：与传统寓言不同，卡森的故事以控诉而非道德训诫结尾。
explanation.evidence: ____47____ (difference) from traditional fables, Carson's story ends with an accusation
explanation.answer: Different。be different from 中的形容词 different 在此作状语，句首需大写。

questions.stem: 第48空

explanation.question: 句意：她教导人们必须承担起保护环境的责任。
explanation.evidence: people must take responsibility ____48____ saving their environment
explanation.answer: for。take responsibility for「对……负责」为固定搭配。

questions.stem: 第49空（warn）

explanation.question: 句意：卡森的主题是一则关于环境破坏的更为沉重的警告。
explanation.evidence: Carson's theme is a more weighty ____49____ (warn) about environmental destruction
explanation.answer: warning。形容词 weighty 后接名词；由不定冠词 a 可知用可数名词单数。

questions.stem: 第50空（employ）

explanation.question: 句意：这种流传久远的简单抒情形式今天依然可以被用来引起人们对重要真理的关注。
explanation.evidence: a simple lyric form that has been passed down through the ages can still ____50____ (employ) today
explanation.answer: be employed。主语 form 与 employ 是被动关系，情态动词 can 后接 be + 过去分词。

sections.partTitle: 第四部分 写作（共两节，满分35分）
sections.secTitle: 第一节 短文改错（共10小题；每小题1分，满分10分）

questions.stem: 假定英语课上老师要求同桌之间交换修改作文，请你修改你同桌写的以下作文。文中共有10处语言错误，每句中最多有两处。每处错误仅涉及一个单词的增加、删除或修改。
questions.material:
增加：在缺词处加一个漏字符号（∧），并在其下面写出该加的词。
删除：把多余的词用斜线（\）划掉。
修改：在错词下画一横线，并在该词下面写出修改后的词。
注意：1. 每处错误及其修改均仅限一词；
2. 只允许修改10处，多者（从第11处起）不计分。

I used to afraid of insects, but last Friday's biology class make a big change in me. In that class, Miss Zhao, our biology teacher, showed we insects on stamps. The bees, butterfly and many other insects looked lovely and beautifully on the stamps. Miss Zhao told us the names of the insects or described their living habits. She even played some recordings of their singing, what was fun. Now, I've come to love those of small living things. In the evening, when I take the walk in the school garden, the singing of insects become more meaningful to me.
questions.modelAnswer:
1. 在‘to’后加上‘be’
2. 把‘make’改为‘made’
3. 把‘we’改为‘us’
4. 把‘butterfly’改为‘butterflies’
5. 把‘beautifully’改为‘beautiful’
6. 把‘or’改为‘and’
7. 把‘what’改为‘which’
8. 删去‘those 后的 of’
9. 把‘the’改为‘a’
10. 把‘become’改为‘becomes’

explanation.summary: 本文是一篇记叙文，作者原本害怕昆虫，上过一节生物课后开始喜欢这些小生命。

points.knowledgeNode: be afraid of / used to do
points.note: 「害怕……」为 be afraid of；used to do sth. 后接动词原形，故须补出 be，即 used to be afraid of。
由 last Friday 可知事情发生在过去，谓语用一般过去时。
作动词 showed 的间接宾语，须用宾格 us。
与 The bees、many other insects 并列，泛指一类，用复数 butterflies。
looked 是系动词，与 lovely 并列作表语，须用形容词 beautiful。
「讲名字」和「描述生活习性」是并列关系而非选择关系，用 and。

points.knowledgeNode: which 引导非限制性定语从句
points.note: 此处为非限制性定语从句，指代前面「播放昆虫鸣叫录音」这件事，用 which；what 不能引导定语从句。
those 可直接修饰 small living things，无须加介词 of。

points.knowledgeNode: 固定搭配 take a walk
points.note: 「散步」为 take a walk，用不定冠词。

points.knowledgeNode: 主语中心词决定谓语数
points.note: 主语中心词是 the singing（单数），of insects 为修饰成分，一般现在时谓语用第三人称单数 becomes。

sections.partTitle: 第四部分 写作（共两节，满分35分）
sections.secTitle: 第二节 书面表达（满分25分）

questions.stem:
你们学校正举办主题为「用英文讲中国故事」的征文活动。请你以一位中国历史人物为题写一篇短文投稿，内容包括：
1. 人物简介及事迹；
2. 意义或启示。
注意：
1. 词数100左右；
2. 题目已为你写好。
questions.modelAnswer:
Confucius is a well-known figure in Chinese history. His teachings emphasized the importance of moral values, respect for elders, and social harmony. Confucius traveled throughout the country, imparting his wisdom to countless disciples and leaving a profound impact on Chinese society.

The significance of Confucius cannot be overstated. His teachings shaped the moral and ethical foundation of Chinese culture, fostering respect for authority, harmonious relationships, and the pursuit of knowledge. Even today, his ideas continue to guide individuals and communities in China and beyond.

Confucius's life offers valuable lessons. He stressed self-cultivation, respect for elders, and the pursuit of knowledge, which serves as a guiding light in our fast-paced and interconnected world. His teachings remind us of the importance of integrity, compassion, and social responsibility.

explanation.summary: 书面表达｜征文投稿（应用文），介绍一位中国历史人物并谈其意义或启示。
explanation.question: 写作要点两条：① 人物简介及事迹；② 意义或启示。题目已给，词数 100 左右。建议三段式：第一段用一般过去时／一般现在时概述人物身份与主要事迹；第二段谈其历史与文化意义；第三段落到对当下的启示，用现在时。人物可选孔子、李时珍、张衡、屈原等，事迹须具体，避免空泛赞美。
explanation.evidence: 词汇积累：著名人物 a well-known figure；强调 emphasize / stress；道德价值观 moral values；社会和谐 social harmony；传道授业 impart his wisdom to disciples；深远影响 a profound impact；不可估量 cannot be overstated；道德伦理基础 the moral and ethical foundation；修身 self-cultivation；正直与同情心 integrity and compassion。
explanation.answer: 高分句型：现在分词作伴随状语 Confucius traveled throughout the country, imparting his wisdom to countless disciples and leaving a profound impact…；否定强调句式 The significance of Confucius cannot be overstated（其意义无论怎样强调都不过分）；which 引导非限制性定语从句 …the pursuit of knowledge, which serves as a guiding light in our fast-paced and interconnected world。可将简单句扩展为复合句，如把 fostering respect for authority… 改写为 which fostered respect for authority…，以体现句式多样性。
